profile.reading: Equinix operates a very large global portfolio and this session found its own per-building pages under equinix.com/data-centers/ to be inconsistently populated: some individual IBX codes 404 entirely (confirmed fresh this session for DC17), and others that do load, such as DC7, checked fresh this session, still omit street address and square footage, deferring that detail to a downloadable specification sheet not reachable by this research pass. Given this, addresses in this batch rely on aggregator sourcing, preferring cases with independent multi source agreement, per this registrys standard source hierarchy. This specific row is an unnamed Equinix building in Torrance, CA per registry data. A prior research pass checked the operators own LA1 building page and confirmed LA1 is a different facility, in downtown Los Angeles, not Torrance, leaving this row unmatched to any Equinix metro code. This session identifies the match: multiple aggregators, DataCenterMap, PeeringDB, Connectbase, Inflect, OCOLO, and datacenters.com, independently and consistently identify Equinix LA7 as the Torrance facility, at 1501 Francisco Street, Torrance, CA, six agreeing sources. An UPSTACK marketplace listing for the same facility includes frmr-vz in its own URL slug, consistent with LA7, like several other Equinix buildings in this registry, likely having originated in Equinix 2017 acquisition of Verizons data center business.

profile.reading: Per the Wikipedia article on the NAP of the Americas, this Miami, Florida building sits at 50 NE 9th Street in downtown Miami and totals 750,000 square feet across 6 stories, described as one of the worlds largest data centers. Now operated by Equinix (as MI1) after Equinix acquired the building from Terremark Worldwide (a Verizon subsidiary) in 2016 for 3.6 billion dollars as part of a 24 data center portfolio deal. The building sits 32 feet above sea level and is engineered for Category 5 hurricane conditions, hosts 160 network carriers, provides peering to AWS, Microsoft Azure, and Google Cloud, and connects to 15 subsea cable landings plus a K-root DNS server. The article does not state a power capacity in MW.

reading:
Equinix, Inc. is a publicly traded real estate investment trust headquartered in Redwood City, California, trading as EQIX, SEC filer CIK 1101239.

The company's own site states a global footprint of 281 data centers spanning metros across six continents, organized into Americas, Europe/Middle East/Africa, and Asia Pacific regions, with more than 513,000 interconnections between customer networks, a figure the site says exceeds its next ten competitors combined, and more than 10,500 customers. The fetched page did not include a founding year, an exact headquarters street address, a megawatt capacity total, or a dollar-denominated construction investment figure.

The registry here tracks 45 Equinix facilities across six states, California, Illinois, New Jersey, Texas, Virginia, and Washington, a narrower US footprint than the company's stated global scale, reflecting Equinix's interconnection-and-colocation business model, in which Equinix builds and operates dense network-exchange facilities in major metro cores rather than the large single-campus buildouts favored by hyperscalers such as AWS or Meta. Equinix's 513,000-plus interconnection figure is a network-density claim rather than a compute or power capacity figure, and it is not directly comparable to the facility counts or MW totals recorded for other operators in this registry.
